title: Finite bounded sublevels of a positive rational lattice form
statement: Let $M$ be a free abelian group with a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], let $V=M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and identify $M$ with its image under the injective map $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Let $B:V\times V\to\mathbf Q$ be a symmetric bilinear form, meaning that it is $\mathbf Q$-linear in each argument and $B(v,w)=B(w,v)$. Assume $B(v,v)>0$ for every $v\ne0$. For every $c\in\mathbf Q$, the set $\{m\in M:B(m\otimes1,m\otimes1)\le c\}$ is finite. The empty basis and negative $c$ are allowed.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62, lattice-in-a-bounded-ellipsoid argument; rational bilinear-form formulation of the linear-algebra input implicit there.

proof.text: Choose the given finite integer basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$. Base change of a free module gives the rational basis $f_j=e_j\otimes1$ of $V$. Thus $m=\sum_j z_je_j$ has $m\otimes1=\sum_j z_jf_j$, with uniquely determined $z_j\in\mathbf Z$. If $r=0$, then $M=\{0\}$ and the assertion holds. Also $B(v,v)\ge0$ for every $v$: it is positive for $v\ne0$ and is zero at $v=0$ by bilinearity. For $c<0$ the sublevel is empty. Hence assume $r>0$ and $c\ge0$.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62; agent-written rational-coordinate expansion of the bounded-ellipsoid argument.

proof.text: Apply the orthogonal-basis lemma over $\mathbf Q$ to the finite-dimensional space $V$ and the symmetric bilinear form $B$. Write its basis as $(u_i)_{i=1}^n$ and put $d_i=B(u_i,u_i)>0$, since basis vectors are nonzero. For $v=\sum_i x_iu_i$, expand bilinearly and use $B(u_i,u_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$ to obtain $B(v,v)=\sum_i d_ix_i^2$.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62; agent-written rational-coordinate expansion of the bounded-ellipsoid argument.

proof.text: For $v=m\otimes1$ in the sublevel, all summands $d_ix_i^2$ are nonnegative, so $x_i^2\le c/d_i$. The elementary inequality $|t|\le1+t^2$ follows by considering $|t|\le1$ and $|t|>1$. Consequently $|x_i|\le R_i:=1+c/d_i$. Expand each $u_i$ in the rational basis: $u_i=\sum_j a_{ji}f_j$, with fixed $a_{ji}\in\mathbf Q$. Comparing coefficients of $f_j$ gives $z_j=\sum_i a_{ji}x_i$. Hence $|z_j|\le K_j:=\sum_i|a_{ji}|R_i$. These nonnegative rational bounds depend only on $B,c$ and the two chosen bases.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62; agent-written rational-coordinate expansion of the bounded-ellipsoid argument.

proof.text: Write each $K_j=p_j/q_j$ with integers $p_j\ge0$, $q_j\ge1$, and take $N_j=p_j+1\in\mathbf N$, so $K_j\le N_j$. Each integer $z_j$ therefore belongs to the explicit list $-N_j,-N_j+1,\ldots,N_j$. Enumerating these lists successively gives at most $\prod_{j=1}^r(2N_j+1)$ tuples. The map $m\mapsto(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ is injective by uniqueness of basis expansion. Thus the sublevel injects into this finite list of tuples and is finite.

source.place: Chapter I, proof of Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62; agent-written rational-coordinate expansion of the bounded-ellipsoid argument.
